author: nsalminen
body:
## Overview
This pull request overhauls the repository structure to resolve GitHub Pages compilation issues and improve maintainability/extendability. Previously, the repository had separate Jekyll setups at the root and in the 2025 subdirectory, causing conflicts that prevented proper Jekyll processing. This setup made it difficult to maintain and extend the website, as new pages had to be manually managed rather than leveraging Jekyll’s templating and collection features.

With this restructure, GitHub Pages can now correctly build the site using Jekyll, enabling full use of templates, includes, and collections. Future updates, including new conference years or additional content types, can be easily integrated by adding subdirectories without requiring a separate Jekyll setup. At the same time, backward compatibility is ensured via automatic redirects, preserving access to previously shared links.

## Key Changes
- The repository now hosts a single Jekyll website at the root, eliminating conflicting configurations.
- Year-specific assets (layouts, includes, data) are organized into subfolders (e.g., _layouts/2025, _includes/2025, _data/2025), enabling easy addition of new years or alternative template structures.
- The 2024 directory remains unchanged with plain HTML.
- The 2025 directory now contains only markdown files. A Jekyll collection defined in the root config processes these files, automatically generating HTML and setting permalinks based on folder structure (e.g., ieeeismar.net/2025).
- Custom permalinks can be set via the permalink property in markdown front matter.
- The redirect_from property (enabled by a plugin) ensures backward compatibility. For example, legacy URLs like /papers.html are redirected to the new /contribute/papers path.
- The homepage redirect is now managed by Jekyll’s configuration rather than relying on a meta tag, resulting in a faster, seamless transition.
